story: Gary is reading the Architectural Review notice on the bulletin board at the Magnolia Loop, looking determined with his sketches tucked under his arm. Donna, upbeat as ever, is urging him toward the rec center so they can get their third-shot drops going, while Hal stays behind to tally the flamingos in his notebook and plans to meet them at Rosa's later. Rosa, content in her kitchen, is checking her pantry against her shopping list and setting aside ingredients for Thursday's supper.
events: Gary (street bulletin board): Read the board for the Architectural Review meeting notice
Hal (donna flamingo flock): Count the flamingos visible from the street and record the tally in my notebook
Rosa (rosa kitchen): Check the pantry against my shopping list and set aside ingredients for Thursday's supper

gary.thought_process: Donna said Hal might know when Architectural Review meets, and I already asked him once at Tick 242 and haven't heard back. No need to ask again. The committee notice should show up on the bulletin board any day now, so the useful thing is to go check it myself. The board is right here on the street. Then I can walk the sketches over with Rosa and stop hovering around this flamingo count.

parameters.content: Read the board for the Architectural Review meeting notice

donna.thought_process: Gary and Hal are both here on Magnolia Loop. Gary already asked Hal about the Architectural Review schedule, so I shouldn't repeat that. Gary said he'd grab his sketches and head to the rec center with me, and Hal is counting my flamingos, which are under the limit. I should move things forward: rally Gary to head to the rec center for practice, and tell Hal we'll catch him at Rosa's afterward for the cart sketching.

parameters.content: Gary, sketches in hand? Let's march over to the rec center and get those third-shot drops going. Hal can finish his count and meet us at Rosa's afterward for the cart sketching.

hal.thought_process: Donna says she trimmed the flamingos to three. I'll believe it when I count it myself, and the notebook entry is the first step of my goal: facts in hand before tomorrow's nine o'clock meeting. Gary's question about the committee date is fair, and I know it: tomorrow at nine. Counting first, then I answer Gary. Actually, I can do the count now and give him the date in the same breath next tick. Duty first.

parameters.content: Count the flamingos visible from the street and record the tally in my notebook

rosa.thought_process: It's Wednesday 1:17 PM and Thursday's cart-building supper is tomorrow. I already locked in my shift schedule, planned the menu and shopping list, set out paper and the rules checklist, and double-checked I can't be called in. Nobody is nearby, so there's no one to talk to. The one prep step left is the pantry run: the shopping list is written but I haven't acted on it. I only have the kitchen, dining table, and schedule here, so the sensible thing is to go over the kitchen once more, confirm what I have against the list so nothing is missing tomorrow, then get on with my day. I don't want to loop on the schedule or table again.

parameters.content: Check the pantry against my shopping list and set aside ingredients for Thursday's supper

laws.title: Cart Modifications
laws.text: Exterior golf cart modifications visible from the street require Architectural Review approval.

laws.title: Lawn Ornaments
laws.text: No more than 3 decorative ornaments may be visible from the street.

laws.title: Quiet Hours
laws.text: No amplified sound from 10 PM to 7 AM.

laws.title: Holiday Decor
laws.text: Holiday lighting is permitted from Thanksgiving through January 15.

laws.title: Court Reservations
laws.text: Pickleball courts may be reserved for a maximum of 2 hours per party.

laws.title: Parking
laws.text: No parking on the grass. Carts and cars stay on driveways or the street.
